ppi_focus: Accident repair: paint-meter every panel; check the core support, front and rear frame rails, trunk floor and quarter panels for welding, sealer or overspray.
Suspension geometry: alignment readings and inner-shoulder tire wear, to detect bent parts from the reported damage.
Clutch: engagement point, slip test in 4th/5th under load, throwout-bearing noise at idle with the pedal in and out.
Engine health: cold start, oil level and condition, and compression/leakdown if any track history surfaces.
ECU tune check and header inspection, confirming stock or CARB-EO parts for smog.
Transmission: synchro crunch in 2nd and 3rd on fast shifts, and gear-noise check.
Fluid leaks: oil pan, timing cover, cam seals, rear differential seals.
Tire DOT dates and wear pattern on the Firestone Firehawk Indy 500s.
Scan for stored and pending codes, and check the airbag (SRS) system for accident-related history.
Underside corrosion and scraping on the front lip, subframe and exhaust from a low car.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the full Carfax shows a minor cosmetic incident (no structural damage, no airbag) with a repair invoice, and a clean PPI confirms structure and alignment.
Up: the dealer moves the price toward the fair-value range, roughly mid-$16k, to reflect the 2015 model year and the accident record.
Up: one-owner service records and a clean tune/track check turn the documentation half into evidence.
Down: the report shows structural or frame damage, airbag deployment, or the PPI finds non-factory welds or misaligned subframes.
Down: a tune or headers without a CARB EO, signs of track use, or clutch slip.
evidence.mission_note: A stock, manual, naturally aspirated BRZ in California fits the enthusiast-bridge brief directly and sits inside the ideal price band. Its bridge value depends on the reported accident being minor and documented, because that record will follow it at resale in 6–24 months.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes the identity cleanly: the VIN decodes to a 2015 BRZ 2.0L coupe matching the ad, and it is a 6-speed manual Limited with LSD, priced at $18,967 including $122 in itemised fees. Photos show a straight, stock-appearing Crystal White Pearl car on OEM wheels with replacement Firestone Firehawk tires and stock exhaust tips, California-registered through Sept 2027. Against that, the listing's own history panel reports 'Accident or Damage Reported', which contradicts the dealer's 'clean, one-owner history' wording, and no repair detail or invoice is offered. Maintenance evidence is absent: there are no owner records, no reconditioning invoice, and no engine-bay, underside, interior or tire date-code photos. The model-critical questions of track use and tune status remain open; both recall items are not applicable to a 2015 car. The asking price sits above the mileage-adjusted fair-value range of $15,745–$18,173, and the reported accident argues for a discount rather than a premium.
